Theme

supplier noun

also suppliers, contractor, purveyor, provider (of goods), vendor (to a business)

classical

Cic. Q. Fr. 2.4.2: redemptōrī tuō dīmidium pecūniae cūrāvī
Cic. Div. 2.47 (Lewis & Short)

redemptor, redemptōris m.

noun, third declension

a contractor, a purveyor: one who undertakes by contract to build, supply or carry out something

The man who has taken a contract (redimere), for a building, for supplies or for collecting a tax; the closest classical word for a firm’s supplier. Christian Latin uses the same word for the Redeemer (Lewis & Short), a sense the context keeps apart. For a single delivery a relative clause is plainer: is quī nōbīs lateres praebet.

Other words

  • praebitor, praebitōris m. — a furnisher, supplier

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 2.53 (Lewis & Short)

    Rare: Lewis & Short has it once in Cicero, of those who furnished what visiting officials needed, and once in Ambrose.

Examples

  • redemptōrī tuō dīmidium pecūniae cūrāvī

    I have seen to it that your contractor got half the moneyCic. Q. Fr. 2.4.2

  • Redemptor lateres nōndum attulit.

    The supplier hasn’t brought the bricks yet.composed

See also supply, seller, company.
